name: SparkFun Qwiic Quad Relay
description: I2C-controlled board with four JZC-11F 5 V SPDT relays (5 A at 250 VAC or 30 VDC each, NO/COM/NC screw terminals). An ATtiny84A running SparkFun's Qwiic Quad Relay firmware drives each relay through an optocoupler and transistor. The logic side runs on 3.3 V (header or Qwiic); the relay coils run on a separate 5 V rail made from a 7-12 V barrel jack supply (about 250 mA with all four on). I2C address 0x6D (0x6C with the ADDR jumper closed, or any 0x08-0x77 set in software). Sold as: SparkFun Qwiic Quad Relay v2.0 (COM-16566), 2 Qwiic connectors plus a 4-pin 0.1" header GND, 3V3, SDA, SCL, a 7-12 V DC barrel jack and four NO/COM/NC screw terminals.
eli5: Four switches for big things (lamps, pumps, fans) that your board flips on and off over two I2C wires.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground (shared by the logic side and the barrel jack sleeve)

pins.name: 3V3
pins.description: Logic supply, 3.3 V: ATtiny84A and the optocoupler LEDs (100 ohm each, up to about 85 mA with all four relays on). Does not power the relay coils.

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data; the board has no I2C pull-up resistors, add 4.7 k to 3.3 V (or use a Qwiic host that has them)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock; the board has no I2C pull-up resistors, add 4.7 k to 3.3 V (or use a Qwiic host that has them)

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Barrel jack centre pin (silkscreen 7-12V): relay supply, regulated on board to 5 V for the coils. About 250 mA with all four relays on. Close the BYP (5V Wall Adapter) jumper only when feeding exactly 5 V.

buildNotes: Commands are single bytes written to 0x6D: 0x01-0x04 toggle relay 1-4, 0x0A all off, 0x0B all on, 0x0C toggle all.
Status: write 0x05-0x08 (relay 1-4), then read; each byte is 0x0F for on, 0x00 for off. Reading 4 bytes after 0x05 returns all four relays.
There is no 'relay N on' command: read the relay's status and toggle only if it is in the wrong state (the driver's on()/off() do this).

Two power systems: 3.3 V on the header/Qwiic for the ATtiny84A, and a 7-12 V barrel jack supply (a 9 V or 12 V wall adapter) for the relay coils. Without the barrel jack the I2C side answers but the relays never click.
The board has no I2C pull-ups; add 4.7 k from SDA and SCL to 3.3 V unless another board on the bus provides them.
Closing the ADDR jumper selects 0x6C; write 0xC7 <addr> to store a new address (0x08-0x77) in EEPROM.
Mains on NO/COM/NC is dangerous: COM to the live wire, NO (off at rest) or NC (on at rest) to the load. Keep fingers off the screw terminals while it is plugged in.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from qwiic_quad_relay import QwiicQuadRelay

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
relays = QwiicQuadRelay(i2c)  # 0x6D; 0x6C with the ADDR jumper closed
relays.all_off()
relays.on(2)
relays.on(4)
relays.on(4)  # already on: on() checks first, so no change
print('R=' + ''.join(str(s) for s in relays.states()))
time.sleep(2)
relays.toggle_all()
print('T=' + ''.join(str(s) for s in relays.states()))
time.sleep(2)
relays.off(3)
print('O=' + ''.join(str(relays.state(n)) for n in (1, 2, 3, 4)))
while True:
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Relays follow on/off/toggle-all commands and report their states

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading (3 difference(s) settled by a third reading with quoted evidence). Not yet tested on real hardware.
